$comment: Issue #250. Every property here is optional, so under --omit-empty=false every one of them is written from whatever the decoder left behind. The first group's zeros are values this schema forbids; the second group's are values it permits, and those must still be written.
title: ForbiddenZeroRoundTrip

tags.$comment: The issue as reported: a nil slice marshals to null, which a typed array forbids.

boundedTags.$comment: The same, where [] would not have been a legal replacement either.

boundedLabels.$comment: The same, where {} would not have been a legal replacement either.

child.$comment: A recursive property is a pointer, whose nil is a null the root forbids.

constant.$comment: No null in sight: the zero of the named string type is "", which the const forbids. This is the re-Validate half.

atLeastTwo.$comment: Constraint-only: an inferred-alias wrapper whose zero marshals as "".

a,b.$comment: A property name no struct tag can carry, so the omission is written by hand.

c,d.$comment: The same, for a zero that is not a null: neither a nil nor an IsZero to recognise it by.

nullableString.$comment: Null is a legal value here, so the property keeps it and an absent one is written back as null.

nullLookingEnum.$comment: The type list admits a null and the enum does not list one, so null is not a value this property may hold. The pointer says otherwise, and under every configuration -- the default one included -- a nil was written back as a null the decoder then refused.

nullLookingBranch.$comment: The same disagreement spelled through an allOf branch.
